Carla (Support): Heads-up — ACME reported intermittent 502s hitting hosted API starting ~09:22 UTC. Error rate ~20% on /v1/generate for a 10m window during a big embeddings job. Sending sample req/resp and traces.

Carla (Support): sample curl

```
curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-****' \
  -d '{"input":"...","model":"rwd-embed-large"}'
```

Carla (Support): response body for failing requests is just `502` with header `x-upstream-error: upstream response error` and empty payload. Request-IDs: req-17f3a, req-17f3b, req-17f3c. No deploys on customer side from them; they say it correlates with them launching 100 concurrent embed workers.

Ben (SRE): Can you paste the exact timestamps for req-17f3a/b/c and any trace/span IDs? Also did we have infra alerts at that time? Any obvious rate-limit or token errors upstream?

Carla (Support): req-17f3a @ 09:22:11 UTC, req-17f3b @ 09:22:12, req-17f3c @ 09:22:13. Trace IDs: trace-0a1b2c (attached). No auth errors, billing looks normal. Customer says when they drop concurrency to 10 things are fine.

Alice (Infra): Looking at frontdoor (L7) logs — we see a tight burst of new connections to the upstream pool, upstream_cx_active spiked from ~40 to ~380 in ~30s on the host group serving embeddings. Envoy metrics: `upstream_cx_overflow` and `upstream_cx_close_notify` counts increased. Looks like connection-pool exhaustion + rapid churn (many short-lived conns).

Alice (Infra): snippet from Envoy stats around 09:22:
```
upstream_cx_active: 380
upstream_cx_total: 24500
upstream_cx_overflow: 340
http_downstream_rq_5xx: 420
```

Dave (Eng): We shipped a small client retry-window change last week that increases parallelism on transient failures. If the SDK starts spinning new TCPs per request (Connection: close) for big payloads, it amplifies fanout. Also saw large POST bodies with `Transfer-Encoding: chunked` — some upstream NGINX workers may be slower to release keepalives.

Ben (SRE): Can we reproduce quickly? Carla, can you run a local stress with headers and payload shape they used?

Carla (Support): Repro steps I used:
1) Generate 100 concurrent jobs using GNU parallel
2) Each job does the curl above with ~600KB JSON payload
3) Run for 1 minute
Command:
```
seq 100 | parallel -j100 'curl -sS -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-****" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d @payload.json'
```
Result: ~18-25% of requests returned 502 within 30s of starting.

Alice (Infra): Quick mitigation applied: bumped frontdoor per-pod upstream max connections (service annotation) from 100 -> 250 and enabled short-term per-tenant burst limit in the router (tenant-burst=20). Also added a conn-pool timeout tweak to recycle stale connections quicker.

infra-bot: No infra deploys in the last 6h. Rolling changes require manual approval.

Alice (Infra): After changes, error rate dropped to ~1.2% in the next 8 minutes. We still see occasional `upstream_cx_overflow` but far lower.

Carla (Support): Customer confirmed improved throughput and lower error rate. They throttled concurrency to 25 and saw steady success.

Dave (Eng): Long-term fixes: (1) patch embeddings SDK to preserve keepalive/connection-pooling for large payloads, (2) add adaptive per-tenant fanout control in the router, (3) add an alert on `upstream_cx_overflow > 50` sustained.

Ben (SRE): Agreed. I'll follow up with runbook updates: add repro snippet and quick mitigations (bump pool, tenant throttle). Assigning ticket to Eng team for SDK change.

Carla (Support): Closing loop with customer now. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
_reserved_note: thread contents are a single continuous string of messages in chronological order as required
